newsitem.title: SWEDEN: U.S. Fidelity keeps increasing in Volvo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fidelity keeps increasing in Volvo.

text.p: U.S. fund Fidelity Investments has been buying shares in Swedish automotive group AB Volvo even after September 30 when it reported holding 36.8 million shares, or 7.9 percent of Volvo equity, a Volvo spokesman said.
"We are in continous contact with Fidelity and the figure I have today is higher," Per Lojdquist, head of investor relations at Volvo told Reuters.
"How high I cannot say. Fidelity handles the external information."
On Monday, newspapers reported that Fidelity held 36.8 million shares, corresponding to 7.9 percent of the equity and 2.1 percent of the votes, on September 30 this year.
Lojdquist welcomed Fidelity as an owner.
"It has been one of my aims to increase foreign ownership in Volvo and there I can say that we have already succeeded," he said.
"We are above bourse average in this respect today."
When Fidelity started buying Volvo shares earlier this year it did not hold any shares in the car maker.
"We have followed Fidelity during this period and we have been in frequent contact all the time," Lojdqvist said.
"We had our first contact with Fidelity on February 22, the day after our annual report for 1995. This was also the starting point for its investment," he added.
